A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Auto Cherry-Picker (ACP) and CLIS. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation-quality experiments, downstream COCO/LVIS and MME/GQA results, scaling experiments and ablations, including supplementary Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation and downstream experiments and adds expanded LVIS comparisons in Table 4 and a human preference study in Appendix 10.

M1.justification: The scene-graph generation, diffusion generation and CLIS filtering procedures remain unchanged. Appendix 6 clarifies existing operations, while ACP‡ varies training-data composition using the existing category-sampling capability.

E1.justification: Appendix 10 adds human participants evaluating generated-image quality and annotation alignment. Existing dataset and downstream-task coverage, including COCO, LVIS, MME, GQA and the HRS spatial examples, is retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds evaluated MosaicFusion comparisons, including its default rare-category setting and an all-category variant, alongside X-Paste. MosaicFusion was previously cited but absent from this comparison. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a distinct human-evaluation protocol: 20 subjects each assess 40 image pairs using two preference questions, yielding 1,535 reported responses. Table 4 also adds a Swin-B comparison and category-composition controls, including ACP‡ incorporating 2K rare images at unchanged total volume. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Human-preference consistency gains a participant study beyond the earlier illustrative examples. Table 4 adds category-composition sensitivity comparisons, and Appendix 12 adds explicit generator failure cases. The existing layout, CLIS-component, LLM-choice and percentile analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance testing for the reported performance. The new preference study supplies participant counts and percentages without uncertainty estimates; these are additions to its protocol and results.

E6.justification: Original table scores are retained, including Table 4's ResNet-50 rows. Expanded Table 4 adds results under new backbone and sampling settings, including ACP‡ rare-mask AP of 21.8 on ResNet-50 and 30.6 on Swin-B. Appendix 10 newly reports 66.1% visual-quality and 94.7% annotation-alignment preference for higher-CLIS images. These are added findings, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the supplementary penalty, normalization and percentile reasoning are unchanged. The added data-prior explanation elaborates existing definitions without introducing new mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: scalable language-driven synthetic data, CLIS quality filtering and downstream benefits correlated with CLIS. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 expands interpretation of overall versus rare-category accuracy through the MosaicFusion comparison. Appendix 12 extends the earlier overlap discussion with explicit scene-graph failures for rare or complex combinations and diffusion failures involving many objects. Existing resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix 6 newly details caption parsing, annotation-box retrieval, grouping and reference-layout selection, plus layout-generator dictionary inputs and outputs. Existing model choices, prompts and training settings remain. Removing the abstract's code promise does not change access information because Section 4 retains the release statement.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Related Work section remain unchanged. MosaicFusion becomes an explicit empirical reference point for positioning ACP's overall and rare-category performance, providing a limited expansion of comparative positioning.

P1.justification: The comparative-results discussion is rewritten, Appendix 6 is renamed and reorganized, and new appendix sections precede the retained visualization section. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains additional rows and separate backbone blocks, and a new four-panel error-analysis Figure 12 is added. Existing figures are retained with some resizing, caption changes and relocation; former Figures 12–15 become Figures 13–16. The overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the earlier illustrative human-alignment evidence with participant judgments, broadens relevant comparisons and clarifies data-prior construction and failure conditions. These improve validation and reproducibility while retaining the original findings. The gains remain limited by sparse preference-study methodology and uncertainty reporting, and an efficiency discussion without measured runtime or cost evidence.
